objective: Sub-goal B145 (G1, question 9), at the coordinator's go-ahead of 2026-11-11 after KNOTS-ALONE-20261111-001: on worlds of three-place knots alone, the not-all-equal law read faithfully (its three-place bonds exactly the world's knots, no ties, nothing frozen) recovers almost every flat surface, but the surface condition was given with the law (A64). Frozen before any run: do d-regular worlds that are not surfaces (a co-knotted pair in one knot or in three or more, or a pinched link) ever read faithfully, for d = 4 to 7? Families: every world on six distinctions, a seeded random sample at 13 to 30 distinctions, and degree-preserving knot swaps of faithful flat tori at 24 to 48. A faithful non-surface world answers no (the surface count is an input); none in range calls for a local lemma with a referee pass. Standalone value relative to the nearest known work: no result found on recovering a hypergraph from the shatter structure of its proper 2-colourings (bounded search: hypergraph reconstruction from colourings appears only in a contextuality setting; weak 2-colourings of pseudomanifolds concern existence, not reconstruction).
stop_rule: One epic: a faithful non-surface world in range, or none in range plus a local lemma with a referee pass; then report and hold.
title: Does a faithful reading supply the surface?
